summary: My SHOULD-FIX landed: the tensions are now enumerated with their owning rows, and I checked those routings against the live cell rather than accepting them. The other repair is one I got wrong at turn 1 — I examined the Blueprint-impact column, judged it still defensible, and cleared it; Codex's ADV-D085-01 says execution is not an architecture hard blocker, and on re-examination that is right, so I have recorded the miss rather than quietly agreeing. I validated the new cell independently: the column's vocabulary already carries non-blocking forms at DR-128/129/130, gate 5 requires removing the cell-level execution bar and this cell was execution-based, and no claim elsewhere in the corpus goes stale. The significant discovery this turn is that file 08 moved under the entry — D-088 landed after dispatch — so the write target's pin is stale. I re-verified all five replacement targets against the new bytes and every one survives verbatim and unique, so the specification still executes. Three notes, nothing blocking.

selfCorrection.summary: At turn 1 I inspected the DR-102 Blueprint-impact column, named it in my verdict as tested, and cleared it. Codex raised it as MUST-FIX ADV-D085-01 and was right.
selfCorrection.theDefect: The live cell reads 'Hard blocker for component protocol blueprint — design contract ACCEPTED (D-015); the hostile-conformance execution half remains, at DR-G21'. I reasoned that it stays true because condition 5 is gated on conditions 1, 2 and 4 and the execution half is condition-4 work, so the blueprint is still blocked.
selfCorrection.whyThatWasWrong: I tested whether the sentence remained defensible in isolation instead of whether it remained consistent with the SATISFIED the same edit installs, and whether gate 5 reached it. D-056 Eligibility (5) requires the MF-6 to remove the cell-level execution or measurement bar, and this cell is execution-based by its own words. Leaving it would have produced precisely the two-live-rules condition the entry's own rejected alternative warns about: a Status column reading SATISFIED beside an impact column reading Hard blocker on the same row. The blocking is relocated to DR-G21 under condition 4, not retained at DR-102.
selfCorrection.theDisciplineIFailedToApply: It is the ADV-D056-01 discipline — verify what an instrument displaces, not only what it does — which I applied to the SATISFIED-bar sentence and did not carry across to the other execution-based statement in the same row. A row has more than one place where a bar can live, and finding one is not finishing the sweep.
selfCorrection.howIVerifiedTheRepairRatherThanDeferring: I did not take the repair on Codex's authority. I surveyed the Blueprint-impact column across all thirty DR-1xx rows and confirmed its vocabulary already accommodates non-blocking and conditional forms — 'Not an MVP blueprint blocker' at DR-128, 'Blocks only a slice that elects…' at DR-129, 'Blocks any slice claiming upgrade continuity' at DR-130 — so the new text is in-vocabulary rather than invented. I then checked the four other documents that mention DR-102 for any hard-blocker claim that would go stale; all three outside file 08 are cross-reference lists, and file 11's mention is 'DR-102 hostile conformance' in a list of work needing executable harnesses, which remains true.

notesNonBlocking.observation: Both pins are stale, and one of them is the write target. file 08 is pinned at ff2ebadd… and now measures 4520ca6bd7d8816e1934f49620c40fb3a1e400ea20d825287b95f4f50187e849; COORD is pinned at 6dd90409… and now measures 85b04187a8410f309ed3e953ca8833d122fbc79add3b45b194ddfe72b5e78efe. I traced the cause rather than reporting the mismatch bare: D-088 was adopted at 94b28c86a773f3e87c6d8fecc56693f508439199 after this turn's dispatch, writing the sixteen harness identifiers. This is not a blocking finding — the table is headed 'at dispatch' and was true then, the entry carries 'If a cited file moves, re-measure', and D-088 is the sibling entry the same coordinator scheduled. But it deserves more weight than the same situation would elsewhere, because a moved write-target digest means the byte-exact replacement specification was authored against bytes that no longer exist. So I re-verified rather than assuming: all five replacement targets — the DR-102 lead, the SATISFIED-bar sentence, the Blueprint-impact cell, the condition-2 Measured now cell and the 'condition 2 remains 0 of 30 SATISFIED' clause — are each still present in the new file 08 verbatim and exactly once. D-088 touched only the twenty-two gate rows and the condition-4 cell, which are disjoint from every target here. Re-pin file 08 to 4520ca6b… and COORD to 85b04187… before adoption.

Turn 1 read 'Does not edit any other cell'; turn 2 reads 'Does not edit any other row'. Cell-level is the tighter constraint, since row-level permits, on a literal reading, other cells inside the two rows already being touched. No reviewer asked for this and neither disposition row mentions it, so it is an unrequested loosening made in a repair turn. I record it as a note rather than a finding because clause 4's heading, 'Exact file-08 edits, and no others', closes the edit set independently, so no new permission is actually created. In an entry that performs the first SATISFIED, the tighter wording is worth keeping. The same turn also drops turn 1's sentence 'It is the first dependent SATISFIED re-record that D-056 named', which was true and located the entry in D-056's lineage; nothing required its removal either.

My turn-1 note D085-N-1 is neither tabled nor addressed — it searches zero times in the subject — and unlike the D-086 case its substance was not fixed in passing. The two replacement targets still treat markdown bold inconsistently: the lead target is quoted with its own '**' delimiters and replaced by text carrying none, while the SATISFIED-bar target is quoted without them, and I confirmed at turn 1 that the delimiters sit outside that match. The existing '**' pair will therefore wrap the new five-sentence bar block. The Blueprint-impact cell added this turn has no delimiters on either side, so it introduces no third variant. Non-blocking, and it does not warrant a further turn, but the recital also compresses my turn-1 verdict to 'OBJECT, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX D085-SF-1' without the note count, so the note is invisible in both places it could have appeared.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Two things are worth stating plainly. The first is that one of this turn's repairs corrects my own error: I looked at the Blueprint-impact column at turn 1, judged it survivable, and said so in my verdict, and it was in fact the second execution-based bar in the same row that gate 5 required displacing. I have recorded that as a self-correction rather than folding it into the general account, and I re-derived the repair's correctness from the column's own vocabulary instead of accepting it because a finding asserted it. The second is that file 08 moved under this entry between dispatch and review, because the sibling MF-6 write landed. For most entries a stale pin is bookkeeping; for this one the pin is the baseline of a byte-exact replacement specification, so I re-ran every target against the new bytes. All five survive verbatim and unique, and the two writes are disjoint. The three notes are re-pinning, an unrequested loosening of a constraint that clause 4 independently holds shut, and a turn-1 note that remains open.
